web-development.title: Web Development and UI/UX Design
web-development.summary: Websites, web applications and digital products that explain what a business does, work properly on a phone and make it easy for customers to get in touch or buy.
web-development.who: Businesses that need a new website, a better one, or a web application their customers or team will use every day.
web-development.problem: Many business websites don’t say clearly what the business does, are awkward to use on a phone, or make it hard to enquire or buy. Visitors leave before they ever get in touch.
includes: Planning the pages, content and the path a visitor takes
UI/UX design for phone, tablet and desktop
Development as a custom build, or on WordPress or Shopify if you want to manage it yourself
Testing across devices and browsers before launch
Launch, and a handover of everything you need to run it

services.title: Website design and development
services.text: Business websites planned around what visitors need to understand, then designed and built to load quickly on any device.

services.title: UI/UX design
services.text: User flows, wireframes and interface design that make a website or product easier to understand and easier to use.

services.title: Landing pages
services.text: Focused pages for a campaign, product or offer, with one clear message and one clear next step.

services.title: E-commerce development
services.text: Online stores designed around how customers browse, compare and buy, from product page to checkout.

services.title: Shopify and WordPress
services.text: Sites and stores on platforms your team can update without a developer, set up and extended to fit how you work.

services.title: Custom web applications
services.text: Portals, booking tools, dashboards and other browser-based software your customers or staff use to get things done.

services.title: Responsive front-end development
services.text: Layouts built for the phone first and refined for larger screens, so every visitor gets the complete experience.

services.title: Redesigns and improvements
services.text: A review of an existing site, followed by the changes that make it clearer, faster and easier to use.

principles.title: Clarity first
principles.text: A visitor should understand what you do, who it’s for and what to do next within a few seconds.

principles.title: Designed for the phone
principles.text: Most of your visitors arrive on a phone. We design for that screen first, not as an afterthought.

principles.title: Easy to maintain
principles.text: Sensible platforms and clean structure, so the site stays easy to update after launch.

faq.q: Do you build custom websites, or use WordPress and Shopify?
faq.a: Both. A custom build suits sites with specific needs or a web application. WordPress or Shopify suits businesses that want to update pages or products themselves. We recommend one at the start and explain why.

faq.q: Will the website work properly on phones?
faq.a: Yes. Most visitors arrive on a phone, so we design for that screen first and test on phones, tablets and desktops before launch.

faq.q: Can we update the website ourselves after launch?
faq.a: Yes. We hand over the logins and notes you need, and choose a platform your team can manage.

faq.q: Do you redesign existing websites?
faq.a: Yes. We review what the current site does well and where visitors drop off, then make the changes that make it clearer, faster and easier to use.

faq.q: Do you also handle SEO or digital marketing?
faq.a: We build sites with search engines in mind: clear page titles and descriptions, fast pages, a sitemap and a clean structure. We don’t currently run ongoing SEO or advertising campaigns.

ai-automation.title: AI Automation
ai-automation.heading: Automate repetitive work. {Give your business room to grow.}
ai-automation.summary: Workflow automation, with AI where it helps, that takes repetitive work off your team: enquiries handled, details moved between tools, follow-ups prepared and reports put together.
ai-automation.who: Businesses where the same manual steps repeat every day: answering enquiries, chasing leads, copying information between tools, preparing updates.
ai-automation.problem: Work gets stuck between tools and people. Leads wait for a reply, customer questions pile up, and someone spends hours moving information from one place to another.
includes: Mapping the current process and where time is being lost
Designing the workflow, including where a person reviews or approves
Building it and connecting it to the tools you already use
Testing it on real cases before it goes live
Documentation, and adjustments once your team is using it

services.title: Lead management and follow-up
services.text: New enquiries captured, qualified, routed to the right person and followed up consistently, so fewer leads go cold.

services.title: Customer enquiry and support workflows
services.text: Incoming questions sorted, answered from your own information where appropriate, and passed to a person when one is needed.

services.title: Sales and marketing workflows
services.text: Research, outreach preparation, content drafts and campaign reporting, with your team approving what goes out.

services.title: Process automation
services.text: Repetitive processes mapped, simplified and automated, so information moves between tools without being re-typed.

services.title: API and tool integrations
services.text: Connections between your CRM, forms, email, spreadsheets and other tools, so information reaches the place it’s needed.

services.title: Reporting and internal tools
services.text: Weekly numbers gathered from your tools and put into one summary, and small internal tools for the steps your team repeats.

principles.title: Tied to real work
principles.text: Every workflow starts from a task your business does today and the time it currently takes.

principles.title: People stay in control
principles.text: Agents handle routine steps. Anything that needs judgement goes to the right person to review.

principles.title: Built around your tools
principles.text: We connect the CRM, inbox, forms and spreadsheets you already use instead of replacing them.

details.heading: Which work is worth automating
paragraphs: The best candidates are tasks your team does often, the same way each time, and that mostly move information from one place to another. If a task needs real judgement on every case, it may suit an AI agent with a person approving, or it may be better left as it is.
points: It happens every day or every week
It follows roughly the same steps each time
It means copying details between tools, inboxes or spreadsheets
Delays cost you something: a slow reply, a missed follow-up, a late report

details.heading: People stay in control
paragraphs: An automation should make your team faster, not hide what is happening. We decide with you which steps run on their own and which wait for a person to approve, and we keep a record of what each workflow did.
Before anything goes live, we test it on real past cases. If a step fails, the workflow stops and tells someone, rather than carrying on with bad information.

details.heading: Working with the tools you already use
paragraphs: We connect the CRM, inbox, forms and spreadsheets you already have, wherever they offer a supported connection, instead of asking you to switch. Where a workflow uses a paid third-party tool or an AI service, we tell you the running cost before we build it.

faq.q: What kind of business is AI automation suitable for?
faq.a: Any business where the same manual steps repeat every day: answering similar enquiries, chasing leads, copying details between tools or preparing the same report each week. Small teams often feel the benefit most, because those hours come out of a few people’s days.

faq.q: Do we need technical knowledge to use it?
faq.a: No. We build and connect the workflow, test it with you and hand over plain notes on how it works. Your team keeps using the tools they already know.

faq.q: Will automation replace our staff?
faq.a: That isn’t the aim. Automation takes on the repetitive steps so your team can spend more time on customers and on work that needs judgement.

faq.q: What happens if an automation makes a mistake?
faq.a: Steps that matter wait for a person to approve them, every run is logged, and a failed step stops the workflow and alerts someone. We also test on real past cases before going live.

faq.q: How is this different from AI agent development?
faq.a: Automation follows the steps you define, with AI helping on parts such as reading or drafting. An AI agent decides how to handle each case within limits you set. Many projects start with automation; we suggest an agent only when the work needs it.

example.title: An example: following up new enquiries
steps: A new enquiry arrives through your website form or email.
An agent reads it, pulls out the key details and adds them to your CRM or spreadsheet.
It drafts a reply using your own service and pricing information, and passes it to your team to approve.
If the customer hasn’t replied after a set time, it prepares a follow-up and reminds the right person.

ai-agent-development.title: AI Agent Development
ai-agent-development.heading: Custom AI agents {built around your business workflows.}
ai-agent-development.summary: Custom AI agents that read incoming work, handle routine cases inside your tools and hand anything unusual to a person, within limits you set.
ai-agent-development.who: Businesses with a steady flow of work that needs reading and a first decision: requests to sort, documents to check, records to update, questions to answer from your own information.
ai-agent-development.problem: Simple automations follow fixed rules, so they break when an email is worded differently or a case doesn’t fit the pattern. The work falls back on your team, and the automation is quietly switched off.
includes: Defining the agent’s job, its limits and what it must hand to a person
Preparing the information it works from: your services, policies and past examples
Building it and connecting it to your tools, with the access it needs and no more
Testing it on real past cases and reviewing the results with you
Monitoring, documentation and adjustments after launch

services.title: AI agents for business operations
services.text: Agents that take on recurring tasks such as sorting requests, preparing documents or updating records, with people reviewing where it matters.

services.title: Multi-agent systems
services.text: Several specialised agents working on a larger process, each responsible for one part, with clear handovers between them.

services.title: Agents with human approval
services.text: Agents that prepare the work, such as a reply, a quote draft or a record update, and wait for a person to approve it before anything is sent or changed.

services.title: Agents that work from your own information
services.text: Agents that answer questions and draft replies using your services, prices and policies, and say so when they don’t know.

principles.title: Clear limits
principles.text: Each agent has one job, a defined set of actions it may take and a list of things it must never do on its own.

principles.title: A person approves what matters
principles.text: Anything that commits your business, such as a price, a refund or a message to a customer, can wait for approval.

principles.title: Every action is recorded
principles.text: You can see what the agent did, when and why, so problems are easy to find and fix.

details.heading: What an AI agent is
paragraphs: An AI agent is software that uses a language model to work through a task: it reads what has come in, decides what kind of case it is, and takes the next step using the tools it has been given, such as looking up a record, drafting a reply or updating your CRM.
Unlike a chatbot, an agent doesn’t just answer questions. It does a piece of work, and it can be set up to stop and ask a person whenever it reaches a decision it shouldn’t make alone.

details.heading: Automation or an agent: which do you need?
paragraphs: If the steps are the same every time, a workflow automation is simpler, cheaper and more predictable. An agent earns its place when each case is a little different and needs reading and judgement before anything happens.
points: Automation: the same input leads to the same steps, every time
Agent: the input varies, and the right next step depends on what it says
Often the answer is both: an automation hands the unclear cases to an agent, and the agent hands the hard ones to a person

details.heading: Where agents fit in a business
paragraphs: Good first projects are tasks with plenty of volume, a clear definition of a good result and a person who can review the output.
points: Reading and sorting incoming enquiries and support requests
Drafting replies and quotes from your own information for approval
Checking documents or forms against a list of requirements
Keeping CRM records and spreadsheets up to date
Preparing research summaries and briefings for your team

details.heading: Security, access and approvals
paragraphs: An agent gets only the access its job needs. We agree with you which actions need approval, keep a log of everything it does, and explain which AI provider processes your data and under what terms before anything is connected.

faq.q: What is the difference between a chatbot and an AI agent?
faq.a: A chatbot answers questions in a conversation. An AI agent carries out a task, such as sorting an enquiry, updating a record or preparing a reply, using the tools it has been connected to.

faq.q: Can an agent work with our existing software?
faq.a: Usually, yes. Agents connect to tools that offer an API or a supported integration, such as many CRMs, inboxes, forms and spreadsheets. We check your tools before we propose anything.

faq.q: Can we control what the agent is allowed to do?
faq.a: Yes. You decide its limits, which actions need a person’s approval and what it must always hand over. Those rules are part of the written scope.

faq.q: Is our business data safe?
faq.a: The agent gets only the access it needs, and we tell you which AI provider processes your data and under what terms before anything is connected. Sensitive actions can always require approval.

faq.q: Do we need an AI agent or a simpler automation?
faq.a: If the steps are the same every time, a simpler automation is usually the better choice. We’ll tell you which fits after looking at the work itself.

business-consulting.title: Business Consulting
business-consulting.heading: Find the bottlenecks. {Build a clearer path to growth.}
business-consulting.summary: Practical growth and operations consulting. We look at how your business wins customers and gets work done, find what’s holding it back, and set out a clear, prioritised plan.
business-consulting.who: Founders and owners of small and growing businesses who know something isn’t working, but not exactly what, or where to start.
business-consulting.problem: Growth stalls for reasons that are hard to see from the inside: a sales process that loses enquiries, work that depends on one person, tools that don’t talk to each other, or too many priorities at once.
includes: A conversation about your goals and what isn’t working
A review of how enquiries, sales and delivery run today
Identifying the bottlenecks and the opportunities worth acting on first
A written, prioritised plan with practical next steps
Help putting it in place, if you want it

services.title: Growth assessment
services.text: A structured look at how customers find you, enquire and buy, and where they drop away.

services.title: Process improvement
services.text: Mapping how work moves through the business, then removing the steps, delays and hand-offs that slow it down.

services.title: Digital transformation strategy
services.text: Deciding which parts of the business should move to better tools or online channels, in what order and at what cost.

services.title: Technology and AI adoption
services.text: Choosing the tools and AI uses that fit your business, and planning how your team will start using them.

principles.title: Practical over theoretical
principles.text: Every recommendation comes with a next step your team can actually take.

principles.title: Honest priorities
principles.text: We say what matters most and what can wait, even when the answer is “not now”.

principles.title: Not tied to our own services
principles.text: If the right fix is a process change or someone else’s tool, the plan says so.

details.heading: Common challenges we look at
paragraphs: Most engagements start from a feeling that the business should be doing better than it is. Usually the cause is one of a handful of things.
points: Enquiries come in but too few turn into customers
The owner is involved in every decision and every task
Work is tracked in inboxes, chats and memory rather than one system
Tools have been added one by one and don’t connect
There is no shared view of what to work on first

details.heading: What a strategic assessment covers
paragraphs: We look at the whole path from a customer’s first contact to the work being delivered: how people find and contact you, how enquiries are handled, how work is planned and done, which tools you rely on and where your team’s time goes. The result is a short written report that names the bottlenecks and ranks what to fix.

details.heading: From plan to implementation
paragraphs: A plan is only useful if it gets done. You can take it to your own team, to another provider, or ask us to carry out the parts we do: a website, a workflow automation or an AI agent. Either way, the plan is yours to keep.

faq.q: What does a consulting engagement involve?
faq.a: A conversation about your goals, a review of how the business runs today, and a written, prioritised plan. The exact scope and price are agreed in writing before we start.

faq.q: Is business consulting suitable for a small business?
faq.a: Yes. Small businesses often benefit most, because a few changes in how enquiries and work are handled make a visible difference to a small team.

faq.q: Will you only recommend your own services?
faq.a: No. If the best fix is a process change, a different tool or another provider, the plan says so.

faq.q: What do we get at the end?
faq.a: A written plan that names the bottlenecks, ranks what to fix first and sets out practical next steps, plus a conversation to walk through it.

faq.q: Can you help put the plan into action?
faq.a: Yes, where it involves what we do: websites, workflow automation and AI agents. For anything else, the plan explains what to look for.
